name: Sess_PitStopUpdateJob_Update
notes: Pit stop update job, vtable slot 3 (ptr 0x1456236b8 in the table at 0x1456236a0; no direct calls). job+0x08 PitStopInstance, job+0x10 float dt. Returns early while PitStopInstance+0x64 is set. At 0x1403c0add it scales dt by PitStopInstance+0x3bc, the crew rate (while job+0x14 is 0 the sequence evaluate at 0x1403c07a1-0x1403c07d4 runs first, and its Start/Stop events can rewrite +0x3bc before that read), runs the PitStopLogic update (+0x330 vt+0x18) with the scaled dt, then Game_PitStopActionObserver_SetTransitionSequence (observer at +0x370). While +0x65 is clear (the transition call is skipped too while it is set) it then rewrites +0x3bc as factor x +0x33c (0x1403c1ab0, 0x1403c1f73), the factor set by the transition at +0x380 (1.0 by default; other transitions use other constants and clamped catch-up ratios); +0x33c is the base rate. Game_PitStopLogic_NeSequenceClipTargetImpl writes the crew speed from the pit lane car record *(pitlane+0x68+car*0x10) into both +0x33c (logic +0x14c, logic at +0x1f0) and +0x3bc on the sequence's Start event; Stop puts both back to 1.0, and so does SetTransitionSequence on every state change or forced call (on both sides of its +0x388 test), so a rate kept in +0x33c lasts only until the next state change, Start or Stop. So a rate written only to +0x3bc applies to the frame that reads it and is replaced at the end of the call; a rate that should persist goes in +0x33c. The scaled dt then advances the sequence instances: the crew sequence +0x3b0 while its flags +0x74 & 0x21 are clear, and +0x398/+0x3a0/+0x3a8 only while the bytes +0x390/+0x391/+0x392 are set (and their flags allow), each by instance+0x5c (the sequence time, float) += scaled dt x global scale (0x146046628) x resource+0x54 (the resource time scale). In game the time runs in seconds (the 1990 pit stop log: the crew speed, written by the Start event at 13/30 s of F1StartJobDoStandardStop258, is already set when the time reads 0.5), so +0x54 is about 1, not a frame rate. The instance's resource is instance+0x08, its name index resource+0x38 (g_Ne_NameTable); the update also reads a second name index at resource+0x3c (0x1403c0d4c).

name: Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting
proto: void Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting(void *contracts, const void *meeting, uint32_t team, uint32_t driver, uint8_t reason, uint8_t notify)
notes: Driver Career contracts manager (DriverCareerContractsManagerComponent): makes the driver's current secret meeting. Finds the driver's DriverSecretMeetings record in contracts+0x3a8..+0x3b0 (16-byte slots, record +0x40 driver key; returns when none). With notify set and the driver the human it posts ProcessSMMessage (vtable 0x145698190, name getter 0x140e04320; +0x10 driver, +0x14 meeting id, +0x18 team, +0x1c reason) through 0x140e0ab40. Then it allocates a 0x24-byte SecretMeeting from contracts+0x210 (vt+0x18, align 0x10), copies the 0x14-byte meeting definition (an entry of contracts+0x298..+0x2a0, 20 bytes) to +0x00, writes reason byte +0x14 = 3 (offered; a constant, not the argument), day +0x18 and weekend +0x1c (the definition's +0x04 percent of the season's weekends through the time component +0x370, 0x141267be0/0x141269000) and team +0x20; when the record already has a current meeting the new one is freed again (vt+0x38) and the old one stays, otherwise it is stored at record +0x18 with the allocator at +0x10 (0x140d7f7fe). Last it adds the meeting day to the career calendar through 0x141269180 (time component +0x370). Only two callers in the KB build: Game_DriverContracts_AdvanceSecretMeeting (0x140d8060f, the next meeting of a series) and 0x140d82710 (0x140d82aa1, after the contracts screen command 0x7388e27d marks the human's contract with removedReason 10); no other code allocates the 0x24 record except the save loader 0x140d730c0 and the online co-op receive 0x140d80630. Raised by laneS (Progressive Career lane S: secret meetings in follow mode).

name: Game_DriverContracts_AdvanceSecretMeeting
notes: Driver Career contracts manager: moves the driver's secret meetings on. Returns when the driver has no DriverSecretMeetings record (contracts+0x3a8..+0x3b0, record +0x40) or when his contract (contract_owner +0x298 list, DriverContract +0x50 driver) is active (+0x2c), its removedReason (+0x12) is not 10, it runs more than one season (+0x20 > 1) and does not end this season (+0x24 != time component +0x428). No current meeting (record +0x18 null): it takes the first meeting definition with id 0 (contracts+0x298..+0x2a0, 20-byte entries), picks a team with 0x140d7f830 (a random team of the driver's rank window, 0x140d80bc0) and calls Game_DriverContracts_OfferSecretMeeting(contracts, def, team, driver, 3, notify). A current meeting with reason (+0x14) 3 (offered, waiting for the player) is left alone. Any other reason (0 declined, 1 accepted, set by the secret meetings view model 0x1422fca00 just before its tail call) is resolved: 0x140d7fe80 works out the next definition id (reason 1 takes the definition's +0x08, 0 its +0x0c and adds the meeting's team to the ignored teams of the offers at contracts+0x3c8; it also updates the driver's 0x5c-byte entries of the component at contracts+0x380 (+0x460), and the reason 1 path ends in 0x14106bf60), the current meeting is moved onto the record's previous meetings (+0x28..+0x30) by 0x140d83cd0, which nulls record +0x18 (0x140d83d72/0x140d83db8), so the vt+0x38 free after it (0x140d803cf/0x140d8041b) finds nothing and the meeting lives on in the previous meetings; then the next definition, when one has that id, is offered (reason 3; a next definition with kind byte +0x10 == 0 after a non-accept gets a newly picked team, otherwise the meeting's team); with no such definition and notify set it posts ProcessSMMessage (vtable 0x145698190, meeting id -1) for the human. Callers: the daily tick 0x14126a1a0 (vtable 0x1456cdee8; its loop over contracts+0x3a8 calls 0x140d7f220 then this with notify 0 at 0x14126b899) and the secret meetings view model command handler 0x1422fca00 (vtable 0x14577dd20; commands 0xe47022a1 sets reason 0, 0xb027c7fd sets 1, then jmp here with notify 1 at 0x1422fcc89). Season change (contracts vtable +0x188, 0x140d76570) frees every current and previous meeting. Raised by laneS (Progressive Career lane S: secret meetings in follow mode).

notes: DISPUTE(V0294). The game's immediate signing (AI renewal 0x140d99210 'Add new driver' / 'Replace old RESERVE driver', auctions 0x140c49310, online negotiation 0x140ff5180). offer is a 0x2c-byte contract record (+0 new team key; +0xc u16 day = clock/1440 and +0xe = flag are written; offer[0..10] is copied into the driver contract in [renewal+0x290]+0x298, setting +0x2c, posting 0x145696e60). It first calls 0x140d8ecd0(renewal, offer, &driver): when the incoming driver sits on another team it backfills his old seat with that team's first reserve (vehicle +0x5e none, +0x80 >= 2): Career_Record_DriverMove(reserve, old team, incoming team, 2) and Career_Set_EntrantData_Thunk(reserve, incoming vehicle, pos|0x100); with no reserve it returns 0 and Sign returns without signing. With replaced_driver set it then records/sets the incoming driver (reason 0) and benches the replaced one (reason 3). The old team does not lose the seat when it has a reserve (wording per V0294). drivers.cpp does not call it

name: Game_Refresh_PerformanceComparison
notes: VEHICLE PERFORMANCE COMPARISON refresh (Team HQ hub and R&D page; callers 0x1418130b0 (the comparison's constructor, rcx = this) and 0x141f40690 (rcx = [rsi+0x960])): zeroes the count (+0x38) and copies 20 entries to +0x40 (0x14 each: team key +0, driver key +4, value +8; keys prefilled 0x3fff0000), then switches on the mode +0x1d0 (0..4, other values return). Modes 0..3 fill the entries with 0x141890e60; modes 1..3 sort them (0x14194d970, or 0x14194c840 when +0x1f7, which asserts through 0x14029b020 when +0x218 is clear); mode 2 keeps the first 3, mode 3 keeps a 3-entry window around the player team; mode 4 computes inline for the player team only (model key == +0x1d4) and sets the count to 1. Every mode ends with a tail jmp to 0x1418914f0 (the R&D performance panel) with rcx = the comparison. 0x141890e60 walks the UpgradesComponent at +0x10 (models +0x298..+0x2a0): per team value = sum of the type metadata rating base (model +0x1a38 entries +0xc, only entries whose department +1 equals +0x1d8 unless +0x1d8 is 5) + 0x143518350 (all departments) or 0x143518660 (one department), the completed upgrades' share of (rating_full +0x10 - rating_base +0xc); the player's team (+0x1f7 and key == +0x1d4/+0x1d6) per driver through 0x143522910 with the driver key at +4. Verifier corrections V1088 folded in.

name: Game_Fill_PerformanceComparison
notes: VEHICLE PERFORMANCE COMPARISON fill, called only by Game_Refresh_PerformanceComparison 0x141890990 for modes 0..3 (0x141890ae8, 0x141890b08, 0x141890b5a, 0x141890bac; rcx = rsi = the comparison) before the sort, the top-3 cut (mode 2), the 3-entry window around the player team (mode 3) and the tail jmp to the panel build 0x1418914f0; returns nothing. Zeroes the count +0x38, then walks the UpgradesComponent at +0x10 (models +0x298..+0x2a0) and appends at +0x40 + count*0x14, incrementing +0x38, with no check against the 20 slots. A team entry writes only +0 (team key = model +0xc) and +8 (f32 value) and keeps the refresh prefill {+0 0x3fff0000, +4 0x3fff0000, +8/+0xc/+0x10 0} elsewhere. Skips: with +0x1f5 set, a model for which 0x141895110(comparison, team key) is true; the +0x1f6 block (career [+8]+0xf08, its list +0x298 stride 0x30 matched to +0x2b0) only skips (0x1418911d2 jne 0x141890f00) and makes no entries. With +0x1f7 and the model key == +0x1d4/+0x1d6 (the player team) the entries are per driver from 0x143522910 (+4 driver key), each valued with its team's model. Value = the type metadata rating base sum (+0x1a38 entries +0xc; department +1 == +0x1d8 unless 5) plus 0x143518350 or 0x143518660 (the completed upgrades' share). The panel's rows stop at +0x38, but its player-reference lookup 0x14189157c-0x141891821 searches all 20 slots for +0x1d4/+0x1d6 whatever +0x38 says and feeds every row's +0xc delta and +0x10 ratio, so a wrap that removes entries after orig lowers +0x38 and refills the vacated slots with the prefill. EA: rva 0x188b3b0, called from the refresh 0x188aee0 at 0x188b038/0x188b058/0x188b0aa/0x188b0fc. Verifier corrections V9288 folded in.

notes: cxx=assignGarageSlotsByPreference; every entrant of a team gets the same garage, slots 0,1,2... The garage is *(garages+8)[garage_index] read with no bound check (callers: Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByTeamOrder's listed-team loop does not check it). The team's entrant with team_position present (EntrantRecord +0x81) and the lowest team_position (+0x80) looks up its driver (0x1423dbcf0, key +0x50) and takes that driver's preferred slot (driver +0xc); the others get 0,1,2... skipping it. Each entrant gets a 0x98-byte record {entrant copy, +0x88 garage, +0x90 slot} pushed to out_assignments and Sess_Set_GarageSlotEntrant_Thunk(garage, entrant, slot) (0x1424a840e, 0x1424a84ec), which ignores slot >= 2: a garage holds two cars.

Groups the entrants by team (Sess_Group_EntrantsByTeam_Thunk), then loop 1 walks team_order (u32 team keys: kind byte, stat id u16 at +2; e.g. the PreviousSeasonTeamStandings order): the team at list position i gets garage index i (ebp, incremented for every list entry) through Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference (0x1424a8983) with NO compare against the garage count (rdi = garage count only sizes the free list); a listed team absent from the session pushes its index to a free list unless it is in fixed_teams. Loop 2 gives each unlisted team the next index while it is below the garage count (cmp at 0x1424a8bf3), else a free index below the count (0x1424a8c2e), else no garage at all. So: a team order list longer than the world's garage vector reads past it (see Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference); teams past the garage count that are not in the list get no garage. out_assignments = {allocator, begin, end, cap} of 0x98-byte garage assignment records; *out_assignments is also the free list's allocator. | Assigns garage slots for one vehicle class: resolves a registry service (key 0x14606ecd8), builds an index list from param_3 and calls Sess_Assign_GarageSlotsByPreference. name: Game_TimeTrialLeaderboard_SelectBoard
notes: Time Trial leaderboard screen model (leaderboard_container binding; self+0x9b0 holds the leaderboard reader, self+0xab0 the track map, self+0xe4a a view flag). Reads game_mode_data.current_game_mode.track_info.current_track and returns 0 when it has no track_file_name; otherwise looks the track up in the map at self+0xab0 (entry +0x78 == track_file_name), builds the board key 'LBV%02u%02d%s' (byte +0xe0 of the leaderboard settings, byte entry+1 of the track, 'wet' or dry from settings.current_settings.tt_weather.value) and searches the board list *(*(reader+0x478)+0x10) (+0x18..+0x20, board pointers) for the board whose name (+0x68) matches it with Ne_Compare_StringNoCase. The search leaves 0 when no board carries the key and the board's rank thresholds (+0x88, +0x98..+0xa0) are read at 0x142fce9e3 with no null check: ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x98 at F1_25.exe+0x2fce9e3 when View Leaderboards is pressed with online services off (empty list). Returns the track_file_name found flag in al. Two callers: 0x142fc8910 tests it (0x142fcaae2), the other ignores it (0x142fcc667). A null track map entry would fault earlier at 0x142fce926 (byte [rbx+1]); not reported.

notes: myteam-g2: Stat-event writer handler for BankAccountTransactionMessage (subscribed in Game_StatEvent_SubscribeMessageHandlers). For transaction types in mask 0x7bdffefe (type byte msg+0x14, maps to stat id via table 0x1458740cc) sums income/expense per day (direction byte msg+0x25) and records them through FUN_143760ca0; used for finance stat events. CORRECTION(V9010): Role right: type byte msg+0x14 against mask 0x7bdffefe, id via table 0x1458740cc, amount msg+0x18, sums income/expense (ledger entry byte +0x11 = 0/1) and calls FUN_143760ca0 = Game_StatEvent_WriteCareerCashTransactions; no bank writes. Field labels are shaky: msg+0x28 is a kind selector (1 = sum ledger via FUN_140c68c90, 2 = day stat via FUN_143760c40), not just a valid flag; msg+0x25 is turned into a tri-state sign (1 -> +1, 0 -> 0, else -1) while the 68310 handler treats the same byte as the notify flag.

name: Ne_Heap_DeallocateNonSmall
notes: ne_memory_heap.cpp deallocateNonSmall. Errors: 0xe line 0x4a1 address outside heap; 0x16 line 0x4a4 'Failed to find address %p in the allocated list' (block header size mismatch); 0x50 lines 0x4ad/0x4af start/end bounding-check buffer corrupt. B26h race-load abort = 0x16. Callers: Ne_Heap_Free 0x143963f5a (heap lock held) and 0x14396b295. Block header 0x10 bytes at ptr - guard - 0x10, guard = heap+0x108 (u64; 0 when the heap has no bounding checks): +0x00 int32 link to the next older allocated block and +0x04 int32 link to the next newer one (in 16-byte units from the header, 0 = none; heap+0x100 is the newest), +0x08 u32 block size = align16(requested) + 2*guard + 0x10, +0x0c u32 requested size. The address range is heap+0x98 (start) and heap+0xa0 (size). It unlinks the block (older.+0x04 = newer, newer.+0x00 = older, both re-relative; heap+0x100 = older when it was the newest) and inserts it into the free tree with 0x143962f10, which writes +0x00/+0x04 as tree links and +0x08 = size/16. A header whose +0x00 does not point at a block whose +0x04 points back makes that unlink write 4 bytes elsewhere and leave the true older neighbour linked to a free block; its later free then loops 0x143962f10 (seen at 22:13, session 20261030-111101).

name: Snd_Request_JobWorker
proto: void Snd_Request_JobWorker(void *worker, uint32_t job_type, uint32_t count)
notes: Wwise job worker request callback (AkJobMgrSettings fnRequestJobWorker; the sound engine init 0x143fbf830 stores its address at 0x143fbf90e; no direct calls). rcx = worker function void(uint32 job_type, uint32 usec), edx = job type, r8d = workers requested. Sets the Wwise max active workers of job types 1 and 2 to the worker count (0x146c64290), then under g_Snd_JobWorkerLock hands each requested worker to an idle worker mailbox (12 of 0x30 bytes at 0x146c63bd0: +0x00 thread id, +0x08 fn, +0x10 wake event signalled by 0x14391cdd0, +0x24 type, +0x28 busy flag; the calling thread's own mailbox is skipped) and queues the rest in g_Snd_JobWorkerOverflow at the first free of 24 slots (loop cmp rax,0x4a8 at 0x143fbdde4), adding 1 to g_Snd_JobWorkerPending per entry. Snd_Run_JobWorkerThread drains only overflow slots 0-11, so an entry queued in slots 12-23 never runs and the pending count never returns to 0.

name: Snd_Run_JobWorkerThread
notes: Audio job worker thread body (12 threads, priority 1). mailbox+0x00 = its thread id. Loop: wait for its wake event (0x14391e3b0); run the mailbox request fn(type, 0) (+0x08 fn, +0x24 type); then while g_Snd_JobWorkerPending != 0, under g_Snd_JobWorkerLock, take the first set flag of overflow slots 0-11 only (unrolled byte compares 0x143fc65ea..0x143fc66e7), clear it, decrement the pending count and run that request outside the lock; finally clear its mailbox busy flag (+0x28). Slots 12-23 of g_Snd_JobWorkerOverflow are never read here (no code reads their flags), so with pending > 0 and slots 0-11 empty every worker spins in that loop.

notes: Sequential-impulse / projected Gauss-Seidel iteration over 0xd0-byte rows: lambda from vdpps(vel,J), accumulated impulse clamped (row+0x94/+0x9c), delta*invMass*J added to 8-float velocity slots (32 B per body, array ctx+0xa0); handles 2-body, 1-body tail passes (counts ctx+0x104/0x10c/0x110); param_3 = iteration count, clears velocity array first. notes: Resolves a g_Vm_Registry node by a dotted path C string and returns a pointer to its node handle (node+8; callers read *ret and link into (*ret)+0x28; &k_Vm_EmptyNodeHandle on a miss). rcx = the registry (g_Vm_Registry), rdx = the path as a plain NUL-terminated char * ('#overrides.teams.badges_broadcast.forceindia_26', 'overrides.teams.badges_broadcast.<label>', view_model_data.*), r8 = the base handle the path is relative to (&k_Vm_EmptyNodeHandle at most callers), r9 = 0 or a zeroed 0x20-byte create record {NeStr *name +0, node handle +8, links +0x10/+0x18}: with it a missing path creates the middle nodes (Vm_GetOrCreate_ChildNode 0x1442b2bf0) and the record gets the leaf name and parent (9 of 2166 sites; 2157 pass 0). A leading '#', or *base == 0 with a non-empty path, starts at *(registry[1]+8); an empty path with *base == 0 returns the empty handle; a NULL path returns base+8 (root+8 when *base is 0). The path is copied into a 0x200-byte local (at most 511 characters, 0x1442b1c20-0x1442b1c39) and split at '.' and '#' (0x145a6fe88), indices at '[' ']', each segment into a 0x40-byte local (63 characters); rdx is not kept, so the caller's string is only read during the call. Register a detachable car part: args (component, callback {fn, ctx} 16 bytes, &node name id, 0x70-byte part descriptor (matrix + extents), float factor). Builds the part record on the stack, resolves the model node (0x1446612a0 with the name id; logs the node name from the name table 0x14618ce18 on a miss, format 0x145bf4637) (car-re fix: 0x1446612a0 is Car_Add_DetachablePart_Thunk, which creates the part and appends it; nothing is logged on a miss, the body just returns; 0x14618ce18 is the name table lock and 0x145bf4637 is '%s_%03d', used after a success to name the sub-pieces) and appends the part to component+0xb0..+0xb8 via the component's allocator ([+0xb8-8] vcall +0x88) (car-re fix: the append is inside 0x1446612a0, allocator fw+0xa8; [fw+0xb8-8] is the part just added and its vtable +0x88 returns its node transform part+0x60, used for the sub-piece distance). 11 calls from the front wing init (0x14465f898 ..). (used by vmknolle parts-detach) | car-re 2026-10-28 L2 (kb:subsystems/car.md#parts): body read on the Steam build.
